extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, inventors, law students, and others interested in U.S. patent claim construction
extracted.subtask_description: Canon of claim construction in U.S. patent law that guides how to interpret multiple claims within the same patent, presuming distinct scope among claims and limiting how claim limitations may be imported. Useful for evaluating claim scope, prosecution strategy, and judicial claim construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that claims differ in scope
rubrics_metrics.description: No two claims in the same patent should be interpreted to cover the same thing. It is presumed that each claim in a patent is different in scope and meaning from all other claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this presumption when construing multiple claims: treat independent and dependent claims as having different scope unless clear evidence indicates otherwise. This is the basic rule of claim differentiation expressed on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of the presumption when dependent claim would otherwise be duplicative
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumption is strongest when a different interpretation would be the only way to make a dependent claim more limiting than the independent claim it refers to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give greatest weight to claim differentiation where construing an independent claim to include a feature would render a dependent claim superfluous or non-limiting; courts favor interpretations that preserve meaningful distinctions between claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine tends to produce broader claim constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of the doctrine generally results in broader constructions of patent claims, because it is most commonly used to prevent defendants from limiting a broad genus claim to the range of embodiments actually disclosed or more explicitly recited in other claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When faced with an argument that a broad (genus) claim should be read narrowly to match specific embodiments recited elsewhere in the patent, invoke claim differentiation to support a broader construction. This is commonly used defensively by patentees and plaintiffs in litigation to resist narrowing interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on patentees using the doctrine to broaden claims
rubrics_metrics.description: However, this doctrine cannot be used by the patentee to broaden claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow patentees to expand claim scope beyond what the claim language permits by relying on claim differentiation as a tool to enlarge claim coverage; the doctrine is not a vehicle for expanding claim scope beyond its proper construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on importing limitations from other claims into an independent claim
rubrics_metrics.description: It is improper for courts to read into an independent claim a limitation explicitly set forth in another claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid importing limitations: courts should not construe an independent claim to include limitations that appear only in dependent claims. See cited authority: Environmental Designs, Ltd. v. Union Oil Co., 713 F.2d 693, 699 (Fed. Cir. 1983).
